reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Nov 10: SPX 7520.93 is 4.13% below its 120-day high, below its 50-day (7672.91) but above its 200-day (7331.08); SMH 483.63 sits in Zone 2 ($470-$505) while NVDA 168.89 has fallen below its $175 Zone 2 floor on 3.1x average volume; VIX 19.46 is rolling over from a 28.18 five-day high, HY OAS 3.34 is calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 3 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: NVDA reclaiming $175 with SMH holding Zone 2 and a confirmed second low would prove the bottom formed while we watched and the Watch stance too cautious; an SPX close below its 200-day (7331.08) would prove the correction is a regime break, not a buyable dip, and voids the probe rungs.

ladder.response: No probe. Tranche A stays void; the watch extends and the next downside reference becomes the SPX 200-day at 7331.08.
ladder.trigger: SMH daily close below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or NVDA daily close below $160

ladder.response: Treat as a bull trap. Do not chase the bounce; any probe opened on the bounce is exited on the failed retest.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7750-7820 failure zone or SMH into 580-600 and closes back below the zone within two sessions

ladder.response: Stand down. Ladder suspended, no probes; reassess as a regime break, not a buyable correction.
ladder.trigger: VIX daily close above 25, HY OAS print above 4%, or SPX daily close below its 200-day (7331.08)

ladder.response: Probe re-arms: Tranche A starter per the deployment ladder (SMH limit $505), sized as a probe, not a full add.
ladder.trigger: NVDA daily close back above $175 with SMH closing at or above $470 and a second low holding above the Nov 10 close

reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce (QQQ +1.27%, TQQQ +3.96%) with NVDA still down 2.08% is the pivot-and-fail setup: the first bounce after a zone-floor break is the trap. Entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a bounce into SPX 7750-7820 or SMH 580-600 that fails confirms the trap; only an NVDA reclaim of $175 with SMH holding $470 turns the bounce into a probe.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is real but contained — SPX 4.13% off its high, above its 200-day, credit calm — yet NVDA has broken below its $175 Zone 2 floor on 3.1x volume, so the probe the SMH Zone 2 print would arm is voided until the leader stops falling. No chasing today's bounce.

themes.counterRead: The rollover narrative has run ahead of the credit and index data — this is concentrated leadership rotation so far, not a confirmed broad break. But the divergence itself is real and worth tracking: if credit flips (HY OAS above 4%), the rotation read collapses into a rollover. Do not price a broad break that credit has not confirmed, and do not dismiss the unwind in the names.
themes.dataAnchor: The index has not confirmed a rollover. SPX closed Nov 10 at 7520.93, only 4.13% below its 120-day high and still 2.59% above its 200-day (7331.08), though below its 50-day (7672.91). Mag7 averages 16.31% off its highs against SPY's 4.1% — a 12.21-point divergence gap — while credit is calm: HY OAS 3.34 and bank lending standards LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold).
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — At Its Hardest Test
themes.narrative: The Mag7 unwind reads as a broad market break: NVDA is 30.6% off its 52-week high, GOOGL 29.7%, META 17.8%, and the AI complex dominates the tape's fear.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS daily print above 4% or the Mag7/SPY divergence gap narrowing below 5 points.

themes.counterRead: The data-ahead read is the setup, not the entry. NVDA's decline is classified ACUTE_CATALYST, not sentiment — the catalyst behind the 'Nvidia in the hot seat' headline is unresolved, and NVDA closed below its $175 Zone 2 floor on 3.1x average volume. A fundamentals-ahead dislocation with an unresolved catalyst and a broken zone floor is a watchlist, not a probe, until NVDA stops falling.
themes.dataAnchor: Fundamentals are moving the opposite way from price. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits 30.6% below its high at RSI 23.9. AVGO is 32.9% below its high with revenue up 55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% free-cash-flow margin. DDOG is 40.7% below its high with revenue up 27.7% YoY, 80% gross margin and $1,001M of free cash flow. LRCX is 49.3% below its high with revenue up 131.3% YoY; ONTO is 48.9% below its high with revenue up 41.5% YoY. Five of the dislocation list's FULL_SIGNAL names are sentiment-driven, not fundamental.
themes.label: AI Stack: Revenue Up, Price Down
themes.narrative: The AI trade is dead: NVDA down 22.7% in a month and 5.47% on Nov 10 alone, SMH down 28.01% from its high, and the whole complex priced as if demand has broken.
themes.watchFor: NVDA daily close reclaiming $175 (top of the broken Zone 2 floor).

themes.counterRead: Insider buying plus a 2.5x price-to-sales ratio argues the trough is being bought by people who know the business, but VST's decline is classified ACUTE_CATALYST and one day of breadth does not clear it. Size this as a watchlist name with a promotion condition, not an add, until the group holds the bounce for a second straight day.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is 30.7% below its high at $131.18 with revenue up 19.1% YoY, $1,318M of free cash flow and a 2.5x price-to-sales ratio — cheap by any standard — and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. BWXT is 47.6% below its high with revenue up 18.3% YoY and positive free cash flow. The group is bouncing today (PWR +4.82%, ETN +2.88%, VRT +2.84%, VST +1.40%).
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power: Insider Buying Into the Cut
themes.narrative: Nuclear power names were the AI trade's second leg and they have given it all back: OKLO down 16.21% in a month, SMR down 17.31%, GEV down 15.23%, CCJ down 12.77%.
themes.watchFor: VST closing above $131.18 with CCJ, OKLO, SMR and GEV positive for a second straight day.

themes.counterRead: The alignment holds only while credit stays calm. A hot print reprices the long end; it becomes a regime break only if it cracks credit. The December FOMC is the hinge: if the repricing turns into HY OAS above 4%, the rates story stops being a valuation headwind and becomes a stand-down.
themes.dataAnchor: Rates and credit agree this is a repricing, not a credit event. The 10-year sits at 4.88% and the 2-year at 4.56% with the 2s10s curve positively sloped at +0.32 (no inversion), the policy rate at 3.88%, 10-year breakeven inflation at 2.2%, and HY OAS contained at 3.34 with bank lending standards LOOSE at 1.7%.
themes.label: Rates: Hot Print, Calm Credit
themes.narrative: October CPI came in hot and the December FOMC (Dec 9) is the next live event — the market believes higher-for-longer is back and rate-cut hopes are fading.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS daily print above 4% or the 2s10s curve inverting below zero.

themes.counterRead: The same leverage that fell 25% in a month bounces 4% in a day — the bounce is mechanical beta, not a bottom signal. A one-day levered bounce while NVDA is still down 2.08% on the day proves nothing about the correction ending; it proves the complex moves fastest in both directions.
themes.dataAnchor: The data matches the narrative — the levered and crypto complex is the deepest drawdown in the book, far beyond the index's 4.13% pullback. Today it is also the fastest bounce: TQQQ up 3.96% on QQQ up 1.27%, with SPY up 0.60% and VIX down 5.24% to 18.44.
themes.label: Levered / Crypto: The Deepest Drawdown, The Fastest Bounce
themes.narrative: Leverage is being washed out: CONL down 48.11% in a month, TQQQ down 24.81%, COIN down 25.65%, BMNR down 23.73%, with BTC down 12.23% and ETH down 16.95%.
themes.watchFor: A second straight up day for TQQQ and COIN with VIX closing under 20.

watchFor: NVDA daily close vs $175 (Zone 2 floor): reclaim re-arms the probe; a close below $160 escalates.
SMH daily close vs $470 (Zone 2 floor) and $505 (Zone 2 ceiling).
SPX daily close vs its 50-day (7672.91) and 200-day (7331.08).
VIX daily close above 25 or HY OAS print above 4% (stand-down lines).
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex: either NVDA reclaims $175 with SMH holding $470 and the probe re-arms, or SMH breaks $470 and the correction extends toward the SPX 200-day at 7331.08. The trigger is NVDA's daily close against $175.
